test_cases.name: reset_values
test_cases.description: Hold reset, then release: check o_halt=0, o_err_illegal=0, o_uart_tx=1, o_sts_done=0, o_result_label=0 (registered level outputs) during and after reset, and that the first executed instruction is fetched from PC 0x0 with all FSMs idle (program at address 0 writes a marker to DMEM, read back via host; first vector/MMIO/UART operations start normally).

test_cases.name: reset_async_assert_sync_release
test_cases.description: Assert i_rst_n_core asynchronously between clock edges while a program runs (outputs return to reset values without waiting for a clock edge, no further DMEM writes) and release it away from the clock edge (no output changes between edges; core starts only after release, within a bounded number of cycles).

test_cases.name: reset_during_activity_abort
test_cases.description: Apply reset in the middle of a vector instruction, an MMIO/APB transfer, a UART frame and a running inference: all control state, CSR values (o_sts_done, o_result_label, ctrl/sts/cycles) and o_uart_tx return to reset values, DMEM/IMEM contents are kept, and the program re-runs correctly from PC 0.

test_cases.name: reset_keeps_memories_host_active
test_cases.description: While reset is asserted, write IMEM/DMEM through the host port (host port not gated by reset), pulse reset repeatedly and read DMEM back: contents are never cleared, host reads still work during reset, the CPU does not alter memories while in reset.

test_cases.name: reset_recovers_from_halt
test_cases.description: After an illegal instruction and after ebreak halt the core, apply reset: o_halt, o_err_illegal and sts.err return to 0 and a new program runs normally.

test_cases.name: rv32i_alu_ops
test_cases.description: Directed and random programs exercising all RV32I register/immediate ALU ops, shifts, slt/sltu, lui, auipc with corner operands; results stored to DMEM and compared with a TB reference.

test_cases.name: branches_and_jumps
test_cases.description: All six branch types taken/not-taken, forward/backward loops, jal/jalr with link values: correct targets, link data, and instructions in the shadow of a taken branch/jump are flushed (no side effects).

test_cases.name: load_store_aligned
test_cases.description: lb lh lw lbu lhu sb sh sw at aligned addresses over all four lanes of DMEM rows: sign/zero extension, partial stores change only the addressed bytes (verified via host DMEM reads).

test_cases.name: load_store_misaligned_no_trap
test_cases.description: Misaligned lh/lhu/lw/sh/sw to DMEM at addr[1:0] != 0: no halt/error; stores use byte enables and data shifted by addr[1:0] with bytes outside the word dropped and no word-crossing split (neighbouring word unchanged); loads return word >> (8*addr[1:0]) with missing upper bytes zero-filled, then the normal sign/zero extension of the access width.

test_cases.name: mul_zmmul
test_cases.description: mul with signed/unsigned corner operands (0, 1, -1, INT_MIN, INT_MAX, random), rd=x0: result equals low 32 bits of the signed product.

test_cases.name: illegal_scalar_div_mulh
test_cases.description: For each of div, divu, rem, remu, mulh, mulhsu, mulhu and unknown/all-zero/all-one opcodes (one program per reset): o_halt=1, o_err_illegal=1, sts.err set, older instructions complete, younger instructions have no effect, PC stops and o_halt stays 1.

test_cases.name: forwarding_and_regfile_bypass
test_cases.description: Back-to-back dependent chains covering EX/MEM->EX and MEM/WB->EX forwarding, same-cycle WB->read bypass at both read ports, store-data forwarding, and x0 always reading 0 (writes to x0 ignored, incl. load/jal rd=x0).

test_cases.name: pipeline_timing_differential
test_cases.description: Using time-to-o_halt of small programs: N independent instructions add exactly N cycles (1 instr/cycle); a load followed by an immediate use costs exactly 1 bubble (same halt time as load + independent instruction + use); branch not-taken adds no stall; taken-branch penalty and dot-product iteration length are logged for information only.

test_cases.name: illegal_in_wrong_path_not_halting
test_cases.description: An illegal instruction and an ebreak placed in the shadow of a taken branch/jump (flushed before commit) have no effect: o_halt and o_err_illegal stay 0 and sts.err stays 0 (read via lw), execution continues at the target; the same instructions on the correct path do halt.

test_cases.name: ebreak_halt_fence_nop
test_cases.description: ebreak: o_halt=1, o_err_illegal=0, sts.err not set, PC stops, o_halt stays 1, older instructions complete; fence executes as NOP with no stall or side effect.

test_cases.name: illegal_system_opcodes
test_cases.description: ecall, csrrw/csrrs/csrrc(+immediate forms), mret/wfi and other SYSTEM opcodes each halt with o_halt=1, o_err_illegal=1, sts.err set; outputs sticky until reset and change only at clock edges (registered level outputs).

test_cases.name: imem_range_data_access_unmapped
test_cases.description: CPU loads/stores to 0x0000_0000..0x0000_7FFF: loads return 0, stores are ignored (code at the target still executes unchanged), no o_halt/o_err_illegal and sts.err stays 0.

test_cases.name: unmapped_cpu_addresses
test_cases.description: CPU accesses at 0x0000_8000, 0x1004_0000, 0x2000_1000, 0x3000_0000, 0xFFFF_FFFC: reads return 0, writes ignored (DMEM/IMEM/CSR unchanged, no aliasing onto DMEM base), no error flag.

test_cases.name: imem_depth_and_fetch
test_cases.description: Host-load code at word 0, word 8191 (0x7FFC) and random words; execute across boundaries and jump to/from the last word: all 32 KB fetchable with 1-cycle synchronous read and no aliasing between distant addresses.

test_cases.name: dmem_depth_and_row_map
test_cases.description: Write distinct patterns to first/last/random DMEM rows via host and CPU, read via CPU and host: 256 KB reachable, no aliasing, lane i of row r at address 0x1000_0000 + 16*r + 4*i, byte-enable stores change only selected bytes, read data valid the cycle after the request.

test_cases.name: vsetvli_vl_computation
test_cases.description: vsetvli/vsetivli for SEW 8/16/32 with AVL 0,1,VLMAX-1,VLMAX,VLMAX+1,1030 and AVL strip-mining loop (16,...,6 at SEW 8): rd returns min(AVL,VLMAX) with VLMAX=16/8/4, vl never exceeds PARA_VLEN/8 (vl width covers 16); rs1=x0 forms.

test_cases.name: vsetvli_zero_zero_keeps_vl
test_cases.description: vsetvli zero,zero with a legal new SEW keeps vl (observed through vse element count) and changes SEW (observed through vadd/vse behaviour), with no VLMAX-preservation check (vl=16 at SEW 8 stays 16 after switching to SEW 32).

test_cases.name: vle_vse_unit_stride
test_cases.description: vle8/vse8/vle32/vse32 at row-aligned DMEM addresses with vl = 0,1,odd,max: exactly vl elements are loaded/stored, vector register tail elements and non-written memory bytes stay unchanged (byte-enable), checked through host reads; probe checks o_mem_req held stable until i_mem_ack and ack arrives at least 1 cycle after o_mem_req rises.

test_cases.name: vle_vse_unaligned_address
test_cases.description: Vector loads/stores at row+1..row+15: the low log2(PARA_VLEN/8) address bits are ignored and the aligned row is accessed (checked through memory contents), no halt/error flag; only the row part of o_mem_addr is checked as significant, the ignored low bits (driven unmodified or cleared) are not checked.

test_cases.name: vpu_access_outside_dmem
test_cases.description: vle/vse addressing IMEM range, MMIO, and unmapped regions: access completes immediately without hang, load yields zeros in vd, store is ignored (IMEM/CSR/DMEM unchanged), no error flag.

test_cases.name: vwmul_vv
test_cases.description: vwmul.vv at SEW=8 with directed (-128*-128=16384, -128*127, 0, 1, -1) and random inputs, vl 1..16: INT16 results across register pair vd/vd+1 equal reference; tail and other registers unchanged.

test_cases.name: vwredsum_vs
test_cases.description: vwredsum.vs over INT16 products of vl<=16 elements with vs1[0] initial value, plus accumulation of 49 iterations (784 elements) at extreme +/- values: signed 32-bit result at element 0 of vd without overflow, other elements unchanged; value-only check (latency not checked beyond the 5-cycle minimum).

test_cases.name: vadd_vsra_vmax
test_cases.description: vadd.vv/vx, vsra.vi/vx, vmax.vx at SEW 32 and 8 with edge operands (wrap, INT_MIN/MAX, shift 0/max, shift amounts above log2(SEW) bits to check masking to 5 bits at SEW 32 and 3 bits at SEW 8), vl varied: results match reference, tail undisturbed.

test_cases.name: vnclip_saturation
test_cases.description: vnclip.wi/wx 32->16 (shift[4:0] 0..31) and 16->8 (shift[3:0] 0..15) with values at and beyond both clamp ends, vxrm=0 round-to-nearest-up: saturates to [-32768,32767] / [-128,127] without wrap, bit-exact with reference.

test_cases.name: vmv_variants
test_cases.description: vmv.v.x (splat, tail unchanged), vmv.s.x (element 0 only), vmv.x.s (element 0 to scalar rd, sign-extended to 32 bits, including negative elements at SEW 8) at SEW 8 and 32; scalar result consumed by the next instruction.

test_cases.name: vector_dispatch_stall
test_cases.description: Vector instructions between scalar instructions: pipeline fully stalled until o_resp_done (no scalar side effect before done), cmd transfer only when valid&ready, i_cmd_valid/instr/rs1/rs2 stable until transfer, o_cmd_ready low while a command executes, o_resp_done a 1-cycle pulse, IDLE->DEC->RD->EXEC->WB->DONE->IDLE and IDLE->REQ->WAIT->DONE sequencing observable via handshakes (and state probes if allowed) with every command, including vsetvli/vsetivli, taking at least 5 cycles from start to o_resp_done, scalar rd written in the done cycle (done AND rd_valid) and usable by the immediate next instruction, back-to-back vector instructions execute one at a time, CPU and VPU never request DMEM in the same cycle.

test_cases.name: vector_in_branch_shadow_flushed
test_cases.description: A vector instruction (vsetvli/vse/vmv.x.s) in the wrong-path shadow of a taken branch is neither dispatched nor executed (vl, vector regs, memory unchanged).

test_cases.name: illegal_vsetvli_vtype
test_cases.description: vsetvli/vsetivli with LMUL 2/4/8/fractional, SEW=64 or reserved vsew: o_halt=1, o_err_illegal=1, sts.err set, no command reaches the VPU (vl unchanged).

test_cases.name: sew_dependent_before_vsetvli
test_cases.description: After reset, vadd/vsra/vmax/vmv/vnclip/vwmul/vwredsum before any legal vsetvli are illegal (halt); vle/vse before vsetvli are not halted; a legal vsetvli makes them legal; reset invalidates the shadow SEW again.

test_cases.name: illegal_sew_combinations_and_vd_alignment
test_cases.description: vwmul/vwredsum at SEW 16/32, vadd/vsra/vmax/vmv at SEW 16, vnclip to SEW 32, widening vd odd: each halts with o_err_illegal=1 and is not dispatched; the legal SEW combinations execute; an odd vs2 of a wide source (vwredsum/vnclip) is not alignment-checked and is not tested for halting.

test_cases.name: illegal_unsupported_opv
test_cases.description: Every OP-V / vector memory form outside the exact legal set (REQ-004/005/008 forms plus vwmul.vv and vwredsum.vs) halts with o_halt=1 and o_err_illegal=1 and is not dispatched to the VPU (one program per reset): vsetvl (register form), vwmulu, vwredsumu, vadd.vi, vsra.vv, vmax.vv, vnclip.wv, vwmul.vx, vmv.v.v, vmv.v.i, vsub/vmul/vand/vredsum/vfadd (unsupported ops), masked forms (vm=0) of supported instructions, vle16/vse16, and mask, segment, whole-register, fault-only-first, strided and indexed loads/stores.

test_cases.name: mmio_csr_word_access
test_cases.description: Aligned lw/sw to ctrl, sts, result, cycles, uart_cfg, uart_tx at interim offsets 0x00..0x14: write/readback, reserved bits read 0 and ignore writes, uart_cfg.baud_div reset 0x06C8, o_sts_done follows sts.done, o_result_label follows result.label, CPU stalled until completion and resumes with correct ack.

test_cases.name: apb_transfer_protocol
test_cases.description: On every MMIO access observe APB signals: SETUP (PSEL only) then ACCESS (PENABLE), at least 3 cycles, PADDR (CPU address minus 0x2000_0000, low 2 bits kept)/PWRITE/PWDATA/PSTRB stable until PREADY, PPROT=0, one outstanding transfer, PSTRB=4'b1111 for aligned sw, dmem_ack low until PREADY (younger instructions do not commit during the transfer).

test_cases.name: mmio_partial_misaligned_write_error
test_cases.description: sb/sh to each CSR (they reach APB, not blocked in the LSU) and sw at addr+1/+2/+3: PSTRB != 4'b1111, PSLVERR sampled with PREADY gives a single 1-cycle o_sts_err_set pulse, sts.err reads 1, no register modified, CPU gets a normal ack (no hang, no halt, o_err_illegal=0); an aligned sw gives no pulse.

test_cases.name: sts_err_set_clear_sources
test_cases.description: sts.err is set by PSLVERR pulse and by an illegal instruction, cleared only by writing 1 (write 0 keeps it, sts.busy/done plain RW unaffected), PSLVERR and illegal instruction in close succession both set it; read via lw and probe.

test_cases.name: start_req_sets_ctrl_start
test_cases.description: One- and multi-cycle pulses of i_start_req (also with CPU polling and idle) set ctrl.start=1 (read via lw), firmware write 0 clears it; pulses during reset have no effect.

test_cases.name: uart_8n1_frame
test_cases.description: Write uart_cfg.baud_div (1,2,3,8,100 and default 0x06C8) and uart_tx.data (0x00,0xFF,0x55,0xAA,'0'..'9') then send=1: o_uart_tx idle high, start bit 0, 8 data bits LSB-first, stop bit 1, each bit exactly baud_div clocks (10 bit times), busy=1 for the frame and 0 afterwards, send cleared when byte taken; back-to-back bytes after polling busy.

test_cases.name: cycles_cnt_window
test_cases.description: Execute single vector instructions of different latency (vsetvli, vle8, vwmul, vwredsum): every command, including vsetvli, takes at least 5 cycles from start to o_resp_done (latency done_cycle - start_cycle >= 5); cycles.cnt equals done_cycle - start_cycle + 1 measured by the TB (inclusive window), holds only the last vector instruction (no accumulation), reads 0 after reset.

test_cases.name: cycles_cnt_independent_of_scalar
test_cases.description: After a vector instruction run a long scalar loop and read cycles.cnt before and after: value unchanged, proving it is not fed by the free-running CPU-side counter.

test_cases.name: host_imem_write
test_cases.description: With i_ld_en=1 in reset: write at 0, 0x7FFC and random addresses with i_ld_byte_en of 4'h1/4'h0/4'hF and addr[1:0]!=0: the whole word at index addr[14:2] is written at that edge, byte enable ignored; writes with i_ld_req=0 or wr_en=0 do nothing; verified by executing the loaded code.

test_cases.name: host_dmem_masked_write_read
test_cases.description: Host DMEM writes with all 16 byte_en patterns over lanes 0..3 of first/last/random rows and addr[1:0] noise: exactly the enabled bytes change, lane = addr[3:2], row = addr[17:4]; reads return the stored word.

test_cases.name: host_read_latency_back_to_back
test_cases.description: Host reads and writes issued every cycle with no gaps (read A0, A1, ..., read-after-write on the next cycle, mixed): o_ld_rd_data carries data exactly 1 cycle after each read request, correct for every request, no handshake or lost access.

test_cases.name: host_miss_addresses
test_cases.description: Host read of IMEM (after writing it), MMIO and unmapped addresses returns 0 one cycle later; host writes to MMIO/unmapped addresses change nothing (CSR outputs, DMEM, IMEM unchanged, no aliasing to DMEM).

test_cases.name: host_ld_en_zero_isolation
test_cases.description: With i_ld_en=0 and reset released, toggle i_ld_req/wr_en/addr/byte_en/wr_data randomly during CPU and vector runs: IMEM and DMEM unaffected, results identical, CPU DMEM timing identical (same halt time as with i_ld_* tied 0, no added cycle in the DMEM path).

test_cases.name: host_ld_en_ownership_checker
test_cases.description: TB assertion active in every test: i_ld_en=0 at every rising edge where i_rst_n_core=1 and de-asserted no later than reset release; the host never accesses DMEM while reset is released; also checks the TB drives host accesses only while in reset.

test_cases.name: param_illegal_rejected
test_cases.description: Elaborate m_soc_top with illegal parameter values (PARA_VLEN 64/192/512, PARA_LANE_COUNT 0/3/16, VLEN=128 with 8 lanes): each must fail elaboration with $error from a generate-if.

test_cases.name: param_legal_elaborate
test_cases.description: Elaborate legal combinations (128 with 1/2/4 lanes, 256 with 1/2/4/8 lanes) without error; localparams LPARA_LANE_W=32, LPARA_VREG_COUNT=32, LPARA_ROW_LB=log2(VLEN/8), LPARA_VL_W=clog2(VLEN/8+1) checked for the default build.

test_cases.name: cfg_v256_row_map_and_vector
test_cases.description: With PARA_VLEN=256: host DMEM row/lane mapping (LB=5, byte_en expansion), vsetvli VLMAX 32/16/8, vle/vse/vwmul/vwredsum smoke vs reference.

test_cases.name: random_scalar_regression
test_cases.description: Seeded (logged) random scalar programs of ALU, mul, load/store, branch with dense hazards compared with a TB reference ISS through final DMEM/register dump; failing seed reproducible.

test_cases.name: random_vector_regression
test_cases.description: Seeded (logged) random legal vector instruction sequences (vsetvli, vle/vse, vwmul, vwredsum, vadd, vsra, vmax, vnclip, vmv) mixed with scalar code compared with a TB reference model through DMEM dump.

test_cases.name: mnist_single_image_system
test_cases.description: Load delivered firmware, weights and one image through the host port in reset, release, pulse i_start_req, wait o_sts_done: o_result_label and DMEM logits bit-identical to golden, UART byte equals '0'+label, o_halt=0 and o_err_illegal=0.

test_cases.name: mnist_100_images_latency
test_cases.description: 100 MNIST images each from reset: labels and logits bit-exact vs golden, every inference completes in fewer than 1,000,000 cycles from start to o_sts_done, no halt/error.

test_cases.name: fsm_unused_encoding_recovery
test_cases.description: Force each FSM state register (m_vpu_ctrl 3-bit unused codes, m_apb_master apbm and m_uart uart unused encodings) to an unused code for one cycle and release: the FSM returns to IDLE, no spurious o_resp_done/PSEL/o_uart_tx activity persists, and a subsequent vector instruction, MMIO access and UART byte complete normally; FSMs are verified in IDLE after reset.

test_cases.name: mmio_subword_misaligned_reads
test_cases.description: lb/lh/lbu/lhu at all byte offsets and lw at addr+1/+2/+3 of each CSR: each read completes without hanging the core, o_halt and o_err_illegal stay 0, no PSLVERR pulse (o_sts_err_set) is produced by a read, registers are unchanged and the following instructions execute; read data and sts.err are not checked.

test_cases.name: mmio_unimplemented_offsets
test_cases.description: lw/sw to unimplemented offsets inside the 4 KB MMIO window (0x2000_0018, 0x2000_0020, 0x2000_0100, 0x2000_0FFC): reads return 0, writes are ignored, the core does not hang or halt and no defined register (ctrl, sts busy/done, result, uart_cfg, uart_tx, cycles) changes; sts.err is not checked for these accesses.

excluded.reason: Connection of i_slverr_en/i_protect_en and generator setting are static inspection items; the PSLVERR behaviour they enable is simulated in TC-039.
The port list and widths of m_soc_top are a static interface check done by elaboration/inspection of the module header; every TB instantiates the DUT by name.
Single clock domain, no CDC and no clock gating is a structural inspection item, not observable by simulation.
Firmware start.S content is checked by inspection of the firmware source, not by simulating the DUT.
Same-address read-during-write cannot occur at m_soc_top (single-port m_dmem, CPU/VPU/host never overlap), so it is verified by the m_dmem block testbench.
Accuracy on 10,000 images is measured on the golden model in Python, not on the DUT.
Branch penalty is an estimate (about 2 cycles), not a hard requirement; the TB only logs it in TC-013.
6-10 cycles per dot-product iteration is a stated goal, not a hard requirement; the TB only logs it in TC-013.
200 MHz is a timing/synthesis goal verified by STA with the SDC, not by RTL simulation.
RTL coding-rule compliance is checked by lint and inspection.
Absence of initial/$readmemh in RTL and the init-file mechanism are coding-rule/tool-flow inspection items.
File location of testbench/model/SVA is a project-structure inspection item.
Existence of a regression script reporting PASS/FAIL is a tool-flow item, not a DUT behaviour.
An illegal vtype never reaches m_vpu_csr from m_soc_top because m_cpu_dec halts first; it is verified by the m_vpu_top/m_vpu_csr block testbench.
